items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: first low poly mech image for the Low Poly Mechs exploration.

Input roles:
Image 1 is the owner's ORIGINAL MECH PHOTOGRAPH and the authoritative design reference. Transform this same mech into a simplified low-poly game-asset appearance.
Image 2 is the earlier neutral front reference, used only as a guide for the straight-on relaxed pose, full-body framing and removal of weapons/equipment.

Requested style change:
Rebuild the visible forms with a deliberately small number of broad flat polygonal planes. Large clean angular armor shells, wedge-shaped helmet, simple blocky chest and limbs, low-sided joint cylinders, restrained single-edge bevels and flat face-to-face shading. Remove dense tiny bolts, grooves, layered trim and fine mechanical greebles. Keep enough large functional joints and armor breaks to identify the design. This should visibly resemble a simply modeled low-poly 3D game asset, not a detailed miniature with matte paint, a wireframe, triangular texture overlay, mosaic or voxel robot.

Preserve:
The same recognizable tall mech proportions and silhouette: broad boxy shoulders, compact angular head, twin long chest columns, narrow articulated waist, separate pelvis, substantial thigh shells, long lower legs and split-toe feet. Keep the charcoal/gray palette, restrained red and brass accents, white double thigh stripe and the main asymmetric painted markings in simplified form. No chibi proportions or new design.

Remove completely:
The handheld gun, BOTH back-mounted weapon assemblies (cannon and triple-tube launcher), the entire arm shield, equipment-specific brackets and attachments, and any external backpack payloads, racks or dangling gear. No replacement weapons, holsters, weapon stubs or props. Preserve the mech's underlying body, structural armor and mechanical joints. Both complete hands visible and empty, fingers relaxed and gently curled.

Presentation:
One single full-body mech, strict level FRONT view, minimal perspective, neutral symmetric relaxed A-pose like Image 2, shoulders level, torso upright, arms slightly away from body, legs evenly spaced, both feet flat on one plane. All hands and feet completely in frame with comfortable margins. Solid white background, even neutral lighting, clean matte broad color areas. No room, floor texture, scenery, cast shadow, wear, labels, inset panels, captions or watermark. Portrait approximately 3:4 image.

items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: v002 PS1-style very-low-poly mech reference image.

Input: the supplied v001 mech is the EDIT TARGET and the guide to its identity, silhouette, proportions, pose, camera and colors.

Primary change: simplify this mech MUCH more aggressively into an authentic early PlayStation 1 era 3D game character. Reduce it to only the major masses that make its shape distinctive. Aim for the apparent geometric complexity of a few hundred triangles for the entire character, with large angular planar faces and extremely economical forms. The current image is still far too detailed. Strip away most of its parts instead of merely making their surfaces more faceted.

Keep the recognizable shape: tall adult-mech proportions, very broad boxy shoulders, small wedge-shaped head between them, TWO prominent long vertical slabs down the front of the chest, a narrow exposed waist, a compact pelvis, broad thigh armor, long lower legs, chunky split-toe feet and long arms hanging slightly out from the body. Keep the silhouette and relative size of these major masses close to the reference.

Simplify each major piece into ONE economical volume: one angular block per shoulder; one wedge for the head; one central torso block with the two plain chest slabs; a single narrow waist connector; simple pelvis; a block each for upper arm, forearm, thigh and shin. Elbows, knees and hips become very simple dark low-sided connectors. Hands become simple chunky mitten-like grippers with a thumb and one grouped finger mass, no individual knuckles or small finger segments. Feet become two simple broad angular wedges with only a central toe split.

REMOVE the fine and medium details completely: bolts, screws, circular ports, knee discs, colored joint rings, pistons, rods, hoses, cables, exhaust tubes, small tabs, brackets, vents, inset panels, chest X grooves, cutlines, edge trim, tiny bevels, stacked overlapping armor layers, logos, emblems, numbers, letters and warning decals. Fill these areas with uninterrupted flat surfaces. No tiny parts anywhere. No replacement decorative detailing. Keep only the broad charcoal/gray color blocks, a few simple muted red or brass color patches, and the two broad white thigh stripes as FLAT painted color, without raised geometry. Most armor should be completely plain.

Rendering: unmistakably coarse low-poly PS1-style 3D geometry with hard angular silhouettes, simple flat or basic vertex shading and plain low-detail color textures. No photorealistic material rendering, metallic shine, detailed textures, ambient-occlusion creases, wear, added triangulation overlay, pixel-art sprite, voxel construction or blurring to fake simplification. Make the geometric simplification clear in a crisp readable image.

Preserve the same level straight-on front camera, full-body framing, neutral symmetric relaxed A-pose, empty hands and blank white background. Keep every part in frame, with both feet flat and comfortable margins. Weapons, back weapons, shield and external equipment remain completely absent. No extra views, captions, polygon counts, wireframes or watermark. One portrait image only.

items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: v004 individual-finger correction for Low Poly Mechs.

Input: the supplied v003b three-quarter action mech is the EDIT TARGET.

Change ONLY BOTH HANDS. Replace the merged mitten/gripper finger masses with proper separate robotic fingers that can wrap around a gun handle, while matching this mech's chunky very-low-poly PS1 design.

Each hand must have exactly FOUR individually separated fingers — index, middle, ring and little — plus ONE opposable thumb. All digits originate correctly from a compact broad palm, without extra or missing digits. Preserve the wrist positions and the overall hand scale relative to the forearms. Fingers should be moderately slim solid rectangular forms, roughly one fifth the palm width each, with useful gaps between fingers, not a single solid finger plate. They are slimmer than the previous merged gripper, but still substantial, sturdy and visually proportional to the heavy angular mech. No thin skeletal rods, spidery fingers, spikes or oversized sausage digits.

Use two or three economical block segments per finger and two simple thumb segments, with obvious basic bend locations. Keep the index finger separate so it could sit on a trigger while the other three wrap around a handle. The thumb sits opposite the fingers to close a functional grip. A relaxed partially open gripping posture, with gentle inward bends, visible separation of all four fingers, and a clear handle-sized opening between fingers and thumb. Orient only the hands slightly as needed to show the digits clearly; do not alter the arms or body pose. Both hands remain EMPTY. No gun or handle prop should be added.

Keep the hands plain, angular, flat shaded and economical in geometry: charcoal/gray fingers and palms with the existing simple red thumb-end accents. No fingernails, round human skin forms, tiny mechanical joints, exposed pistons, bolts, panel lines or fine detail. Functional separate fingers are the only added complexity.

Preserve EVERYTHING ELSE exactly: the same character, full body and proportions, broad boxy shoulder blocks, wedge head, twin chest slabs, narrow waist, pelvis, broad thigh armor, long shins, split-toe feet, broad charcoal/gray colors, simple red/brass accents and white double stripe on the same thigh. Same three-quarter camera, grounded staggered action stance, image layout and white background. Same PS1-style low-poly flat surfaces and lighting. No restoration of weapons, shield, backpack or equipment. Do not redesign the torso or add fine details elsewhere.

One full-body portrait image only, both complete hands and feet fully in frame, no inset panels, captions, labels or watermark.

Add the missing fourth/little finger along the outer edge opposite the thumb. Do not count the thumb as one of the four fingers. Do not duplicate thumbs.

Make all FOUR finger chains and their four separate fingertip silhouettes visible on EACH hand. Rotate the wrists just enough toward the viewer and mildly separate the fingers so no finger is hidden behind another. A gently curled, partially open gun-gripping hand posture with four individually countable fingers. No gun or prop. Keep a useful opening between the four fingers and the opposed thumb. Four narrower fingers should fit across the same palm rather than enlarging the whole hand. Make the individual fingers slightly narrower than in this first edit, around one fifth the palm width, but still solid and angular enough to suit the heavy mech. Middle finger longest, index and ring slightly shorter, little finger shorter. Use only two or three simple rectangular segments per finger and two thumb blocks. No fine joints, rods, cables or knuckle greebles.

Preserve the same compact broad palm, wrist scale, charcoal/gray hand colors and red thumb tips. Simple faceted PS1-style forms, no human skin, fingernails, rounded smooth anatomy or skinny skeletal digits.

Keep EVERYTHING outside the hands and wrists unchanged: identical mech design, body and armor, proportions, three-quarter camera, action pose, full-body composition, shoulders, chest, waist, hips, limbs, feet, white thigh stripes and other colors. No new armor detail, weapons, shield or equipment. Same pure white background and even lighting. One full-body portrait image, all parts in frame, no insets or labels.

Final check before rendering: near hand = FOUR clearly separate fingers + ONE red-tipped thumb. Far hand = FOUR clearly separate fingers + ONE red-tipped thumb.
